:::{#rem-quadratic-form-scalar}
#### Like the derivative of $cx^2$

This operation is like taking the derivative of $cx^2$ with respect to $x$ in non-vector calculus:
$\deriv{x} (cx^2) = 2cx$,
and @thm-quadratic-form says $\deriv{\vb} (\tp{\vb} \matr{S} \vb) = 2 \matr{S} \vb$.
For example, with $p = 1$, $\matr{S} = (3)$, and $\vb = (\beta_1)$,
$\tp{\vb} \matr{S} \vb = 3\beta_1^2$,
and its derivative is $6\beta_1 = 2 \matr{S} \vb$.

:::
